source: វិទ្យាការទប់ស្កាត់ និងកម្ចាត់សមាសភាពបទព្រុងលើដំណាំទុរេន (Prevention and Control of Harmful Organisms on Durian), Cambodian technical extension document compiled with reference to CABI Crop Protection Compendium and durian pest/disease literature, 28pp
text: Durian stem borer (Batocera rufomaculata DeGeer) is a large longhorn beetle whose larvae tunnel into the trunk and main branches of the durian tree, feeding on the wood; a heavy tunneling infestation weakens the structural strength of the trunk/branch, can girdle and kill the affected limb, and creates entry wounds that invite secondary fungal infection of the stem tissue. Signs of infestation include sawdust-like frass pushed out of small holes in the bark and sometimes visible sap oozing from entry points. General control approach: inspect trunks and main branches periodically for entry holes and frass, physically probe and remove larvae from shallow tunnels with wire where accessible, and treat deeper tunnels with an appropriate insecticide injected or pushed into the hole before sealing it with mud or wax to trap the insect inside; badly infested limbs beyond saving should be pruned out and destroyed.
